items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I said, “don’t put it in there, give it to me and I’ll sing it.” ... by Jimmy Lunceford.

ctx.x: That’s right, times were tough and there were, my father and my mother and 15 children. Twelve boys and three girls in the depression. So it was very, very difficult. So I didn’t have nickel to buy popcorn, and a dime to go into the movie theater. With all my brothers and sisters you know my father just couldn’t afford to give everybody a dime to get in and a nickel to buy popcorn. So we all had to find some way of finding 15 cents on Saturdays to go to the movies. And so my brothers would go out and get what we…

by Jimmy Lunceford. I said, “don’t put it in there, give it to me and I’ll sing it.” And they couldn’t’ resist that. So you know they would give me the nickel and I would say [scats]. I would sing the whole thing — solo and all — and the whole place would be —

items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I also admired Jimmie Lunceford’s band, because they dressed well. I saw them one time in Toledo in a show

ctx.x: Yeah, I think he did. But I mean that’s what he wanted. He just wanted to approach Fletcher’s orchestra. That makes you want to go back and listen to Fletcher again. But © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

that was a clean band. They were beautiful. And Jimmie Lunceford’s too, he also admired Jimmie Lunceford’s band, because they dressed well. I saw them one time in Toledo in a show — they had three costume changes. They opened up in white tails, they came back in the middle in orange tuxedos, and they closed in light tan tuxedos. Great show band, it was really fantastic. A really good looking outfit too, and entertaining, very entertaining.

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’d say, “What are you going to play?” They’d say, Yard Dog Mazurka by Jimmie Lunceford.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. I would stand if front of this jukebox. People would come up, and I’d say, “What are you going to play?” They’d say, Yard Dog Mazurka by Jimmie Lunceford. I said, “Give me the nickel. I’ll sing it for you.”
